abstract: Today, 1.6 million more women than men are enrolled in four-year colleges and universities in the US, raising concerns that college-educated women will struggle to find suitable partners. This column presents evidence that college women have in fact sustained relatively stable marriage rates, in part by increasingly marrying non-college men. This pattern, combined with the economic decline of non-college men, has reduced the pool of economically stable partners for non-college women. The findings raise the question of whether policies that improve outcomes for less-educated men could also narrow class gaps in marriage and family formation.
abstract_zh: 如今，美国四年制学院和大学中，女性入学人数比男性多出160万，引发了对受过大学教育的女性难以找到合适伴侣的担忧。本专栏提供的证据表明，大学女性实际上维持了相对稳定的结婚率，部分原因在于越来越多地与非大学男性结婚。这一模式，加上非大学男性经济状况的下滑，减少了非大学女性中经济稳定伴侣的储备。研究结果提出了一个问题：改善教育程度较低男性境遇的政策，是否也能缩小婚姻和家庭形成中的阶级差距。
authors: Clara Chambers, Benjamin Goldman, Joseph Winkelmann
title: The marriage squeeze: How the college gender gap is reshaping who marries whom
title_zh: 婚姻挤压：大学性别差距如何重塑婚配格局
